question:
A 45-year-old male with well-controlled HIV (undetectable viral load, CD4 count 475 cells/mm³) is
admitted to the hospital. He presents with a 10-day history of severe rectal symptoms including pain,
urgency, and mucopurulent discharge. The patient has a history of genital herpes and takes daily
valacyclovir for suppression. His sexual history reveals unprotected receptive anal intercourse with
multiple new male partners over the past year. Physical examination reveals: - Temperature: 36.8°C -
Blood pressure: 126/70 mm Hg - Heart rate: 90 beats/minute Laboratory findings show a leukocyte
count of 9000/mm³ (normal: 4500-11,000). Which infectious agent is the most likely cause of this
patient's proctitis? Answer Choices: (A) Herpes simplex virus (B) Cytomegalovirus (C) Campylobacter
jejuni (D) Treponema pallidum (E) Lymphogranuloma venereum (F) Shigella species (G) Human
papillomavirus (H) Gonorrhea (I) Herpes simplex virus that is resistant to valacyclovir (J) Chlamydia

trachomatis (non-LGV)
 A. Herpes simplex virus that is resistant to valacyclovir
B. Gonorrhea
C. Lymphogranuloma venereum
D. Human papillomavirus
E. Chlamydia trachomatis (non-LGV)
F. Herpes simplex virus
G. Shigella species
H. Treponema pallidum
I. Cytomegalovirus
J. Campylobacter jejuni
